gaps.sentence: I will note the reference number in case I ___ it later.
gaps.hint: in case means as a precaution
gaps.explanation: 'In case' describes a precaution and takes the present simple: need.

gaps.sentence: If the walls ___ soundproofed, we would not hear the neighbours.
gaps.hint: unreal present with the subjunctive were
gaps.explanation: Unreal present conditions formally take 'were': were.

gaps.sentence: If the temperature ___ below freezing tonight, the race will be postponed.
gaps.explanation: First conditional: present simple in the if-clause, will + infinitive in the result.

gaps.sentence: If the route ___ safer, I would cycle to work.
gaps.hint: an imaginary present situation, subjunctive were
gaps.explanation: Unreal present conditions formally take 'were' rather than 'is': were.

gaps.sentence: I wish we ___ longer, but our train leaves at six.
gaps.explanation: 'Wish' plus 'could' expresses regret about present ability: could stay.

gaps.sentence: He wouldn't be so tired today ___ so late last night.
gaps.explanation: Past condition with present result: if + past perfect, would + infinitive.

gaps.sentence: As long as nobody ___, we will finish before lunch.
gaps.hint: as long as plus a present verb
gaps.explanation: 'As long as' clauses take the present simple: objects.

gaps.sentence: ___ harder, she would have passed the exam.
gaps.hint: inversion replaces if in formal English
gaps.explanation: Formal English can drop 'if' and invert: Had she studied harder, she would have passed.
